content: Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and thioridazine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Similarly, hydroxychloroquine sulfate and thiothixene also increase the QTc interval, necessitating the same caution. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the effectiveness of the tick-borne encephalitis vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, making this combination contraindicated. Additionally, immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and tisagenlecleucel both enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative. Tocilizumab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate also amplify immunosuppressive effects, posing a similar infection risk, and should be avoided. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and tofacitinib increase each other's toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, requiring avoidance or substitution. Similarly, hydroxychloroquine sulfate and tongkat ali increase immunosuppressive effects and infection risk, necessitating caution. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and toremifene both prolong the QTc interval, and this combination should be avoided. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of vaccines for traveler’s diarrhea, cholera, typhoid, and varicella virus due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, making these combinations contraindicated. Immunosuppressants further increase infection risk when used with live vaccines. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and trimipramine also prolong the QTc interval, requiring avoidance or substitution. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases the effectiveness of the typhoid polysaccharide and live vaccines, as well as the zoster live vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated. Immunosuppressants used with live vaccines further increase infection risk. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ustekinumab amplify immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk, and should be avoided. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and vandetanib both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or substitution. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and vardenafil also increase the QTc interval, requiring caution. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the varicella virus vaccine live due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, making this combination contraindicated. Immunosuppressants further increase infection risk when used with live vaccines. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and vemurafenib both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or substitution. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled, voriconazole, and vorinostat all increase the QTc interval, requiring caution or substitution. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ziprasidone also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the zoster vaccine live due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, making this combination contraindicated. Immunosuppressants further increase infection risk when used with live vaccines. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases immunosuppressive effects, while astragalus decreases them, creating an unclear interaction. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and bupivacaine implant may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia when combined with other drugs that cause this condition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to immunosuppressive effects, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the dengue vaccine due to immunosuppressive effects, requiring close monitoring. Immunosuppressive therapies, such as radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids, may reduce the immune response to vaccines. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and denosumab require caution due to increased infection risk in immunosuppressed patients. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and deutetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval, but the clinical relevance is dose-dependent. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases the effects of insulin and other antidiabetic drugs, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and isavuconazonium sulfate both decrease immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases immunosuppressive effects, while maitake decreases them, creating an unclear interaction. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and mavorixafor both prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and mercaptopurine amplify immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases methotrexate levels by an unknown mechanism, potentially reducing renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ozanimod both increase immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ponatinib both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases the efficacy of sipuleucel-T due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. Preand post-colonoscopy ECGs are recommended for patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate also increases hydroxychloroquine sulfate toxicity via QTc prolongation, requiring similar precautions. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and tobramycin inhaled both increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ublituximab amplify immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and valbenazine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and voclosporin both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the zoster vaccine recombinant due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the effectiveness of this vaccine. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases praziquantel levels by an unspecified mechanism, but the clinical significance is unclear. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and yellow fever vaccine interactions are not clinically significant, as antibody responses remain unaffected.
